items.headline: DESI strengthens the case for looking beyond constant dark energy
items.source_name: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory / DESI Collaboration
items.external_summary: DESI's first three years of data remain consistent with ΛCDM on their own, but combinations with CMB, supernova, and weak-lensing data strengthen the preference for models in which dark energy evolves with time. The reported preference depends on the dataset combination and remains below the conventional discovery threshold.
items.why_it_caught_attention: SAT/H(s)H currently has an active cosmology reconstruction concerned with separating an H0-like large-scale expansion contribution from a c-like shell-time or radial-growth contribution. A changing effective expansion history is therefore a natural external comparison target, without presuming the mechanisms are the same.

items.headline: The clearest gravitational-wave signal yet sharpens tests of the Kerr black-hole picture
items.external_summary: GW250114 was an exceptionally loud binary-black-hole signal. Ringdown and full-signal analyses found the remnant consistent with the Kerr black-hole spectrum and produced unusually stringent single-event tests of general relativity.
items.why_it_caught_attention: Ravel's current Kerr line explicitly uses standard Kerr/Kerr-Newman geometry as a control before asking what survives in the very different particle-scale, over-extreme regime and what—if anything—belongs to H(s)H interpretation. A precision black-hole Kerr measurement therefore sharpens the external control side of that comparison rather than directly testing the particle-scale construction.
